title: Riverbank concat batcher: session-coalescing heuristics for streaming chat
creator: Priya Karthik
description:
Problem: Streaming chat workloads exhibit high per-token variance in sequence lengths and KV cache locality. Current microbatcher either prioritizes latency (many tiny microbatches) or throughput (large coalesced batches) but lacks a middle-ground that preserves streaming latency SLOs while reclaiming GPU memory by better KV placement and slab allocation.

Goal: Design and implement a novel batch formation heuristic ("Riverbank concat") that coalesces in-flight streaming turns across sessions based on time-deadline alignment, KV-hotness affinity, and slab-compactness scoring to reduce GPU memory footprint and improve token throughput without regressing p50/p95 end-to-end streaming latency.

Success metrics (measured on canary cluster):
- p50 end-to-end token latency: <= +5ms from baseline
- p95 end-to-end token latency: <= +30ms from baseline
- GPU memory headroom increase: >= 8% on 80% of nodes
- Token throughput improvement (tokens/sec/machine): +12% relative to current adaptive microbatcher
- KV eviction rate decrease for active sessions: -18%

Scope and constraints:
- Must integrate with existing KV cache manager APIs and not require schema changes to KV slot format.
- Should be parameterizable per-customer (dedicated vs hosted) and per-tier (SLA).
- No changes to model kernels or attention internals. Focus is on scheduling and memory placement.

Design overview: Riverbank concat uses three orthogonal signals to form a microbatch:
1) Deadline alignment window: each in-flight streaming turn carries a soft deadline (based on client RTT + server compute estimate). We introduce a small elastic window (default 12ms) to accumulate turns whose soft deadlines fall into the same window.
2) KV-hotness affinity: maintain a lightweight per-session Bloom counter and a 3-tier hotness state (cold/warm/hot). Warm/hot sessions prefer being co-located to enable KV slot sharing and reduce duplicate hot entries across slabs.
3) Slab-compactness score: compute a heuristic score for a candidate batch that estimates GPU slab fragmentation if the batch is scheduled on a target GPU. Score combines token length variance, KV overlap fraction, and estimated padding cost. Batches below a compactness threshold are preferred.

Heuristics and algorithms to implement:
- Riverbank Window Collector: time-bucketed queues keyed by (deadline_bucket, affinity_bucket). Periodically (every 3ms) flush buckets based on latency budget or when slab-compactness improves by X%.
- Affinity bucketing: group sessions with overlapping KV fingerprints. Use a 64-bit fingerprint of recent KV keys (rolling xor) to approximate overlap cheaply.
- Soft-gating policy: if GPU free memory drops below soft-quota (configurable), relax deadline window and greedily prefer compact batches to avoid early KV spills.
- Prefetch-on-join: when a marginal session is added to a batch and predicted to be warm, issue a low-priority KV prefetch to reduce miss latency; prefetches are cancelable and back-pressured by network budget.
acceptance_criteria: 1) End-to-end integration tests passing in staging with streaming enabled; 2) Benchmark harness shows p50/p95 within targets and improves throughput and GPU memory headroom; 3) Feature flag gateging implemented and safe rollout plan; 4) Observability: per-batch compactness, KV hit/miss, prefetch counts, and slab fragmentation metrics emitted to console; 5) No increase in error-rate or timeouts during a 48-hour canary at 20% traffic.
implementation_notes:
- Add new scheduler component 'riverbank_concatenator' under runtime/scheduler. Keep it behind feature-flag runtime.batch.riverbank.enabled (default=false).
- Integrate with kv-manager: add a read-only endpoint to query session fingerprint and hotness state. No schema mutation.
- Add slab estimator util that mirrors GPU allocator's eviction heuristics to compute compactness score with low overhead (budget 200ns per candidate).
- Prefetch uses existing async KV prefetch path; add priority=low and cancel token.
- Expose per-GPU soft-quota via node-config to allow Dedicated customers to tune conservatively.
- Add unit tests for compactness scoring, integration tests for prefetch cancellations, and e2e perf harness runners.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Over-coalescing could increase tail latency during bursty phases. Mitigation: enforce hard deadline cutoffs and p95 telemetry-driven automatic window contraction.
Risk: Bloom-fingerprint collisions send unrelated sessions together increasing padding. Mitigation: fall back to slab-compactness check and limit batch sizes for low-confidence buckets.
Risk: Prefetch traffic could overload KV backend. Mitigation: global prefetch throttle with adaptive rate limit tied to kv-backend queue length.
rollout_plan:
- Stage 1 (feature off): deliver code + unit tests to main and merge.
- Stage 2 (staging flag on): canary internal traffic 1% for 48h; run perf harness and verify metrics.
- Stage 3 (canary 20%): enable for a subset of hosts in prod for 72h; observe p95 and error rate.
- Stage 4 (ramp): increase by 20% every 24h if metrics stable.
- Stage 5: GA when stable for 7 days and meets success metrics.
Rollback: immediate global flag off and drain in-flight batches; run draining policy to prevent double-scheduling.
